papers.title: GATE EE 2026 Trend-Based Mock Paper 1
papers.description: Balanced mix of core EE topics with emphasis on Machines, Power Systems, and Control Systems. High-frequency PYQs from 2021–2024.
papers.predictionRationale: This paper emphasizes Electrical Machines (highest weightage at ~14 marks) combined with Power Systems and Power Electronics (~22 marks combined). Control Systems stability questions are placed strategically. Network Theory forms the foundation for several circuit-based questions. NAT questions test numerical precision in Power Electronics and Control Systems.

papers.title: GATE EE 2026 Trend-Based Mock Paper 2
papers.description: Focus on Circuit Theory, Power Electronics, and Network Analysis. Includes tricky NAT questions from recent sessions.
papers.predictionRationale: Built around Circuit Theory and Network Analysis as the backbone, with Power Electronics chopper/inverter questions forming the core. Digital Electronics sequential circuits feature prominently. Signals & Systems Laplace transform questions test analytical ability. Complex problems combine multiple concepts — typical of recent GATE trends.

papers.description: Emphasis on Analog & Digital Electronics with solid Signals & Systems coverage. Moderate difficulty with conceptual MCQs.

papers.title: GATE EE 2026 Trend-Based Mock Paper 4
papers.description: Comprehensive revision paper combining all major EE subjects. Mix of easy recall questions and challenging multi-concept problems. Ideal for final practice before the exam.
papers.predictionRationale: Heavy Machines paper: Transformer equivalent circuits, induction motor torque, and synchronous machine alternator problems form the core. Power Systems fault analysis (symmetrical components) and load flow are tested. Control Systems root locus and Bode plot questions assess frequency-domain skills.
